summary: Task 2 implementation is clean and faithful to Decisions 2/15/16. Sha256Hex is a properly sealed utility (final + private throwing ctor + single static method); WebhookSecretVerifier is a @Component using MessageDigest.isEqual with defensive null/empty/malformed-hex handling and zero secret logging; BotService.connect now calls Sha256Hex.hex and the private duplicate is gone. The bonus TokenService refactor tightens the 'one SHA-256 site in main/' AC — grep confirms a single match in Sha256Hex.java. Tests cover every case listed in the task. No critical or major findings.

suggestions.suggestion: Decode storedHashHex BEFORE invoking Sha256Hex.hex(headerSecret). When the persisted hash is malformed, the current order still spends a full SHA-256 cycle on the header before returning false. Reordering (decode stored first → return false on IllegalArgumentException → only then hash header) preserves all current semantics and shaves a redundant hash on the corrupt-state path. No security or correctness impact — purely a micro-cost cleanup.
suggestions.benefit: Avoids a redundant SHA-256 computation on the corrupt-persisted-state path.

suggestions.suggestion: The candidate side is hex-encoded by Sha256Hex.hex and then immediately hex-decoded back to bytes for the MessageDigest.isEqual call. Functionally fine (HexFormat is cheap, output is guaranteed valid hex) but the round-trip reads odd. Two options if you want to clean it up later: (a) compute the candidate digest as raw bytes inline (small duplication of the SHA-256 primitive — would violate Decision 15's single-site rule, so reject), or (b) add Sha256Hex.hexBytes(String): byte[] returning the raw digest and have hex(String) call HexFormat on its result. Out of scope for this task; flagging for future consideration only.
suggestions.benefit: Eliminates an encode-then-decode round trip on the hot path.

suggestions.suggestion: mocked.verify(() -> MessageDigest.isEqual(any(byte[].class), any(byte[].class))) uses the default 'times(1)' semantics. Consider being explicit: mocked.verify(() -> MessageDigest.isEqual(any(byte[].class), any(byte[].class)), times(1)) — documents intent and prevents a silent regression if the call site is ever invoked more than once.
suggestions.benefit: Makes the invocation-count expectation explicit for future readers.
